questions.text:
QUESTION ONE: MOMENTUM AND CIRCULAR MOTION

Titan is the largest of Saturn's moons. For the sake of this question, you can ignore the gravitational effects of the other moons of Saturn and the rest of the objects in the solar system, and assume that Titan is in a perfectly circular orbit.

Mass of Saturn: 5.68 × 10²⁶ kg
Radius of Saturn: 5.82 × 10⁷ m
Mass of Titan: 1.35 × 10²³ kg
Distance between the centres of mass of Saturn and Titan: 1.22 × 10⁹ m

Show that the centre of mass of Saturn and Titan is 2.90 × 10⁵ m from the centre of Saturn.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Calculated with either substitution into an equation or equation with unrounded answer. Working: x_com = (m₁x₁ + m₂x₂)/(m₁ + m₂) = (5.68 × 10²⁶ × 0 + 1.35 × 10²³ × 1.22 × 10⁹)/(5.68 × 10²⁶ + 1.35 × 10²³) = 289895 ≈ 2.90 × 10⁵ m.

questions.text:
Two ice particles around Saturn move toward each other, as shown below. Particle A has a mass of 2.45 kg and a velocity of 8.00 m s⁻¹; particle B has a mass of 3.20 kg and a velocity of 15.0 m s⁻¹. The particles collide and stick together without losing any mass.

Calculate the size and direction of the momentum of the two particles when they are stuck together.

Determine the direction relative to the initial velocity of particle A.

A diagram may assist your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: p_tot = 51.8 kg m s⁻¹, 67.8° anticlockwise from the initial direction of A.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Calculated ONE of: correct momenta for A and B, labelled momentum vector diagram with correct orientation of vectors, correct angle only, total p = 67.6 kg m s⁻¹ if linear addition. Merit: Calculated correct answer (size and angle from A). Excellence: Calculated correct answer (size and angle from A). Working: p_A = 2.45 × 8.00 = 19.6 kg m s⁻¹ (to the right). p_B = 3.20 × 15.0 = 48.0 kg m s⁻¹ (downward). p_tot² = 19.6² + 48.0² = 2688.16. p_tot = 51.8 kg m s⁻¹. tan θ = 48.0/19.6. θ = 67.8° anticlockwise from initial direction of A.

questions.text:
Calculate the time it takes for Titan to complete one orbit of Saturn.

You could begin by calculating the velocity of Titan in its orbit.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Showed F_c = F_g (some evidence of understanding) OR showed v = 2πr/T. Merit: Showed v² = GM/r either algebraically or as part of numerical working OR correct method to find T with incorrect v. OR F_g = 3.4383 × 10¹⁶ N. Excellence: Correct answer with units. Or correct T with use of v = ωr. Working: F_c = F_g. mv²/r = GMm/r². v² = GM/r = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ × 5.68 × 10²⁶ / 1.22 × 10⁹ = 5572.59 m s⁻¹. v = d/T = 2πr/T. T = 2π × 1.22 × 10⁹ / 5572.59 = 1.375569 × 10⁶ s. T = 1.38 × 10⁶ s.

questions.text:
Future manned missions to the solar system are most likely to be launched from space stations in low earth orbit, similar to the International Space Station. Astronauts on the International Space Station appear to be weightless, even though Earth's gravity is still acting on them.

Explain why astronauts appear to be weightless yet can remain in orbit.
questions.expectedAnswer: To maintain a circular orbit, an object requires a centripetal force directed toward Earth's centre
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Stated one of: freefall, no reaction force, F_g provides F_c (can be written as F_g = F_c but must be contextually correct). Merit: 2 complete bullet points OR one complete and two partial. Excellence: Full explanation.

questions.text:
QUESTION TWO: ROTATIONAL MOTION

Rihari and Jane are playing on a roundabout (sometimes known as a merry-go-round) in the local playground. The roundabout has a radius of 1.30 m. Rihari stands on the roundabout whilst Jane pushes on it to make it spin as shown in the diagram. Starting from rest Jane steadily accelerates the roundabout so that it takes 12.0 s to make 4.00 rotations.

Show that the angular velocity of the roundabout after the 12.0 s is 4.19 rad s⁻¹.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Calculated with either substitution into an equation or equation with unrounded answer. Working: θ = ((ω_f + ω_i)/2)t. 4.00 × 2π = (ω_f/2) × 12.0. ω_f = 4.1887 = 4.19 rad s⁻¹. Could also use θ = ω_it + ½αt² with ω_f = ω_i + αt. α = 0.35 rad s⁻².

questions.text:
Rihari then drags his foot along the ground to bring the roundabout to a stop over 19.2 s.

Calculate the average torque exerted to slow the roundabout, if the roundabout and Rihari have a rotational inertia of 430 kg m².
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Calculated ONE of: correct angular acceleration, correct torque using wrong angular acceleration (τ = Iα). Merit: Calculated correct torque. Working: ω_f = ω_i + αt. 0 = 4.1887 + α(19.2). α = −4.19/19.2 = −0.218166 rad s⁻². τ = Iα = 430(−0.218166) = −93.81 ≈ −93.8 N m. Negative indicates torque is slowing the roundabout.

questions.text:
Jane has a mass of 52.0 kg. She runs at 6.39 m s⁻¹ and jumps onto the stationary roundabout, close to the edge, landing 1.20 m from the axis of rotation, as indicated in the diagram.

The roundabout and Rihari have a rotational inertia of 430 kg m².

The rotational inertia of a point mass is I = mr².

Calculate the angular velocity of the roundabout after Jane has jumped on.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Calculated ONE of: L of Jane, I of Jane. If used Jane's L and I, ω = 5.325 rad s⁻¹. If used I = 430, ω = 0.927 rad s⁻¹. Merit: Minor error (correct method). Must have reference to the inertia of roundabout and Jane in L_f. Excellence: Correct working and answer. Working: L_Jane = mvr = 52.0 × 6.39 × 1.20 = 398.736. I_Jane = mr² = 52.0 × 1.20² = 74.880. I_T = 430 + 74.88 = 504.88. L_i = L_f. 398.736 = 504.88ω. ω = 0.79 rad s⁻¹.

questions.text:
Later, Rihari and Jane are both standing on the edge of the roundabout while it is rotating at a constant angular velocity.

Rihari moves inwards, towards the centre of the roundabout.

Explain the effect this has on the rotational kinetic energy of the system.
questions.expectedAnswer: As Rihari moves inward, his mass is closer to the axis of rotation, so I (∝ mr²) decreases.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognised I decreases OR recognised that angular momentum is conserved so angular velocity increases. Merit: Two concepts explained correctly with links. Recognised that due to movement of mass inwards, angular velocity/rotational kinetic energy increases. Excellence: All four concepts explained and linked.

questions.text:
QUESTION THREE: SIMPLE HARMONIC MOTION

Rihari is playing with a ball on a string and lets it swing as a pendulum. It is 1.20 m from the fixed point of the string to the centre of mass of the ball. The top of the string is held, and the ball is released from the starting position at an angle of 5.60° from the vertical. The mass of the string is insignificant compared to the mass of the ball.

Show that the maximum displacement of the ball is 0.117 m.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct answer using sin. Working: sin θ = A/l. A = 1.20 sin 5.60° = 0.117099 ≈ 0.117 m.

questions.text: Show that the angular frequency of the ball's motion is 2.86 rad s⁻¹.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Calculated correct period. Or with wrong T, worked out ω (show question required evidence of understanding). Merit: Calculated ω with correct working and answer. Working: T = 2π√(l/g) = 2π√(1.20/9.81) = 2.197536 s. ω = 2π/T = 2π/2.197536 = 2.859195 = 2.86 rad s⁻¹.

questions.text:
After the ball is released from the starting position, calculate the time it will take for the ball to reach a point 3.30 cm before its next stationary position, as shown in the diagram.

A reference circle may be used to calculate your answer.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Calculated ONE of: correct displacement y (−0.084), reference circle with phasors in correct start and finish positions, used trig for angle past equilibrium θ = 0.801 rad or 45.9°. If two errors: max grade is A. Merit: Calculation with one error, e.g. calculation used correct method with incorrect amplitude or displacement. Or θ correctly calculated as 2.3734 rad and incorrect calculation of t. Excellence: Calculated correct answer. Working: y = −0.117 + 0.033 = −0.084 m. x = A cos(ωt). −0.084 = 0.117 cos(2.86t). cos(2.86t) = −0.084/0.117. 2.86t = cos⁻¹(−0.084/0.117). t = 0.82924 ≈ 0.829 s.

questions.text:
Rihari holds the end of the string between his fingers, and moves his hand horizontally from side to side. He notices that at a certain frequency of movement, the ball will oscillate with a very large amplitude.

Explain why this occurs.

Your answer should include both force and energy considerations.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: States ONE of: resonance, hand is applying driving force, hand is adding energy to the system, friction removes energy from the system, force 'in time' adds energy to system / increase A, f ≈ f₀. Merit: Forces: frequency of driving force matches the natural frequency linked to increased amplitude. OR Energy: when f = f₀, this increases the E_k (lin) of the system, leading to an increase in E_gp and so A increases. Excellence: Complete answer.
